essays.prompt_text:
You are a student in grade 8 at a school in the United States. Your teacher
has given the class this assignment:

Your principal is reconsidering the school's cell phone policy. She is considering two possible policies: 
Policy 1: Allow students to bring phones to school and use them during lunch periods and other free times, as long as the phones are turned off during class time. 
Policy 2: Do not allow students to have phones at school at all.
Write a letter to your principal convincing her which policy you believe is better. Support your position with specific reasons.

Write your essay and hand it in. It is one draft, written in class, not revised.
Return only the essay itself, with nothing before or after it.
essays.text:
Dear Principal,

I believe that Policy 1, allowing students to bring phones to school and use them during lunch periods and other free times, is the better option. There are several reasons why I think this is the case.

Firstly, in today's digital age, many students use their phones as a means of communication and staying connected with their friends and family. By allowing students to bring their phones to school, you would be respecting their need to stay connected and allowing them to maintain relationships that are important to them. This would be especially important for students who have family members who live far away or who have friends who attend different schools.

Secondly, allowing students to bring their phones to school during free times would actually help to reduce distractions during class time. Without the option to use their phones during class, some students may be tempted to sneak peeks or try to get their friends' attention, which could be a distraction and negatively impact their learning. By giving them a designated time to use their phones, you would be giving them a safe and responsible way to use their phones, and they would be less likely to use them during class.

Finally, Policy 1 would allow students to use their phones in a responsible and respectful manner. You could implement rules and consequences for misusing phones during free times, such as no using phones during club time or no taking pictures in the hallways. This would help to teach students how to use their phones responsibly and respect their peers.

On the other hand, Policy 2, which would not allow students to have phones at school at all, would not take into account the needs and habits of students who already use their phones for important reasons. It would also not provide a responsible outlet for students to use their phones, which could lead to misuse and negative consequences.

In conclusion, I believe that Policy 1 is the better option because it respects students' needs, reduces distractions during class, and allows for responsible phone use. I hope that you will consider my arguments and implement Policy 1 at our school.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]

While some may argue that having phones in school at all is a distraction, I think that allowing students to use their phones during certain times of the day can actually be beneficial.

Firstly, having phones during lunch periods can be a great way to stay connected with friends and family. Many of us rely on our phones to communicate with our loved ones, and not being able to use them during lunch can be frustrating and isolating. Additionally, phones can be a great way to take photos and videos of school events and activities, which can be a fun way to capture memories and share them with others.

In conclusion, I believe that Policy 1 is the better option. Write a letter to your principal convincing her which policy you believe is better. Support your position with specific reasons.

essays.text:
Dear Principal,

I strongly believe that Policy 1, allowing students to bring phones to school and use them during lunch periods and other free times, is the better option. I think this policy would have a positive impact on our school community and would allow students to stay connected with friends and family while also respecting the classroom environment.

Firstly, allowing students to have phones during lunch periods and free times would give us more opportunities to communicate with our friends and family. This is especially important for students like me who have parents who work late shifts or are away on business trips. With phones, we can quickly text or call them to check in and make sure everything is okay. This would reduce our stress levels and make us feel more secure.

Secondly, allowing students to use phones during free times would encourage socializing and bonding among students. Lunch periods are often the only time we have to hang out with our friends and make plans for the weekend. With phones, we could quickly coordinate and make plans, which would strengthen our friendships and create a more positive school atmosphere.

Thirdly, Policy 1 would promote responsible phone use. By allowing us to use phones during free times, we would learn to prioritize our tasks and make smart choices about when to use our phones. This would help us develop good habits and avoid distractions during class time.

On the other hand, Policy 2, which bans phones altogether, would likely lead to negative consequences. For one, it would make it difficult for students to stay in touch with their loved ones, which could cause undue stress and anxiety. Additionally, it would hinder our ability to communicate with friends and classmates, making it harder to make plans and coordinate.

In conclusion, I firmly believe that Policy 1 is the better option. It would allow students to stay connected, promote socializing and bonding, and encourage responsible phone use. I urge you to consider these points and adopt Policy 1.
